title: Protestants do not calumniate Rome by charging image-adoration—Councils anathematize the contrary
source_text: III. Unde liquet, Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae immerito queri de Protestantibus, quod Ecclesiae Romanae tribuant imaginum adorationem, quasi, scilicet, istud calumniosum esset. Quaenam enim est calumnia, si Ecclesiae Romanae tribuamus id, quod non tantum ejus schola faciendum esse docet, sed quod ipsa in suis Conciliis facere se protestatur, & sub anathemate recte & pie fieri decernit?
pass_a_gloss: Whence it is plain that the Doctors of the Roman Church complain without desert of the Protestants, because they attribute to the Roman Church the adoration of images, as if, namely, that were calumnious. For what calumny is it, if we attribute to the Roman Church that which not only her school teaches ought to be done, but which she herself in her Councils protests that she does, and under anathema decrees to be done rightly and piously?
pass_b_english: Rome’s own school teaches image-adoration; her Councils anathematize refusal.
Calling that adoration is not Protestant slander—it is Rome’s self-description.
